newsitem.title: UK: Euro Veg Oils - A tight crop buoys rape oil.
newsitem.headline: Euro Veg Oils - A tight crop buoys rape oil.

text.p: Reduced oilseed rape crops in Europe and Canadian coupled with increasing demand have pushed rape oil to a five guilder premium over soy oil in recent days on the European vegetable oil market.
At the close of business on Tuesday Nov/Jan rape oil was offered at 100 guilders against 95 guilders for the same position in soy oil.
Some rape oil crushers are having difficulties with supplies of seeds and are finding their margins being squeezed as farmers become more reluctant to sell seed on a rising market.
"Rapeseed and its products are no longer seen as a substitute for soybean and the market has taken on a life of its own as demand increases," said a trader.

Traders said that environmentalist concerns about genetically-modified soybeans in the United States may have been reflected in some reluctance about using soyoil in Germany. "There was always the potential for rape oil to go to a samll premium over soy oil owing to the lower crop...(this) is exaggerating the situation, if only temporally," one said.
But others said they felt it was perhaps just being used as an excuse to push up rape oil prices on an already-tight market.

On the remander of the European vegetable oil market news has been fairly thin with the outlook for palm oil remaining bearish despite some hit-and-run buying by the Indonesians on the Malaysian market.
"The Indonesian home market is tight and they have been raiding the Malaysian market in the early part of this week. But as soon as prices started to rise they disappeared," said a trader.
On Wednesday data issued by Malaysian cargo surveyor Societe Generale de Surveillance (SGS) put local exports for September 1-25 at 528,150 tonnes compared with 537,175 in Aug 1-25.
Lauric oil prices are slightly up on the week, but trade has been slow and mainly between dealers.
